title: DC-area forecast: Nor'easter to bring periodic showers this weekend
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Clouds build before shower chances increase this afternoon. Highs reach the mid- to upper 60s.

What’s next? Showers at times tonight and again tomorrow. Increasing sunshine and warmer weather after Monday.

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: At least the morning is dry before shower chances increase this afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Saturday): Some sunshine early gives way to mostly cloudy skies by afternoon. With a nor'easter meandering offshore, a few light showers are possible as soon as late morning, mainly east of DC. Showers become more numerous during the afternoon, progressing from east to west. Highs reach the mid- to upper 60s. Winds increase to 15 to 20 mph during the afternoon, with gusts up to 30 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: Intermittent showers continue into the overnight hours, most numerous east and northeast of DC. More spotty showers could reach western areas at times. Lows slip into the mid- to upper 50s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Sunday): Mostly overcast skies stick around, with cool highs only reaching the low to mid-60s. Showers remain possible, especially north and east of DC, but dry intervals are also likely. Northwest winds are near 15 to 20 mph, with occasional gusts over 25 mph. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Skies remain mostly cloudy, with some leftover showers still possible, especially north and east of DC. Lows dip into the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Skies are mostly cloudy Monday as highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s. Breezes gradually decrease. Confidence: Medium

Skies start to clear Tuesday, with a mix of sun and clouds continuing into Wednesday. Highs climb back into the mid- to upper 70s both days, with light winds around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 26

Intense late-season heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 96 degrees, capping a brutal summer marked by persistent 90s and a historic drought.
